newsitem.title: USA: Most stock index futures end down after choppy day.
newsitem.headline: Most stock index futures end down after choppy day.

text.p: Most U.S. stock index futures ended lower after a very choppy session spent battered by profit-taking and technology sector weakness.

Late in the day, local short-covering pulled June Standard and Poor's 500 futures from session lows, but the contract still ended lower on the day. Traders said stock index futures were due to stall after recent huge gains, but they said the overall market tone was firm.
June S&P 500 futures sailed to a fresh two-month high on Friday amid good volume and an increase in open interest.

On Monday, the contract set a new record high at 838.00, again on brisk volume and a rise in open interest. In overnight trade, June reached 838.40, but was unable to challenge that level in Tuesday's day session.
Traders said action was brisk on the day, with price boards showing an estimated June S&P 500 volume of 79,000 contracts.
"We had a lot of weakness in the Nasdaq and we had some divergence because the blue chips were positive," an S&P trader said. "But tech stocks kept their pressure down and we succumbed," he added.
Traders said a sluggish T-bond futures tone after disappointing three-year note auction results also lent bearishness to S&Ps.

The Treasury sold $17 billion in three-year notes at an average yield of 6.438 percent with a stop of 6.449 percent, a "tail" of one basis point. The bid-to-cover ratio was 2.08 and non-competitive bids totalled $967 million.
Some called the day's S&P 500 activity consolidation after a recent steep rally. Since June S&Ps bottomed April 14 at 738.25, the contract has rallied more than 100 points to a record high.
At the close, June S&P 500s were down 1.75 pts at 834.85, Value Lines lost 2.50 to 732.50, Nikkei rose 235.0 to 20,125.0, Russell lost 2.60 to 363.90, and Nasdaq fell 18.35 pts to 924.50.
